name: Maintenance Maturity Not Evidenced
applicable_contexts: utility symptom visible before maintenance maturity is bounded
trigger_conditions: maintenance logs, PM proof or downtime history unresolved
critical equipment or support systems plausible
anti_triggers: preventive program and downtime history are already bounded
physical_basis: Weak maintenance execution can increase utility intensity, stress equipment and distort the apparent root cause of cost or performance issues.
operational_basis: Reactive work orders, poor lubrication, weak PM and missing proof often hide behind what looks like a pure energy problem.
financial_mechanism: Downtime, scrap, failure cost and asset stress can dominate economics before direct utility savings do.
typical_false_assumption: Visible utility cost is the main problem, so maintenance is secondary.
hypothesis: The visible issue may be partly or primarily a maintenance-maturity problem rather than a standalone efficiency problem.
rival_hypotheses: utility intensity is structurally rational for the operating duty
maintenance burden is non-material to economics
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: maintenance proof is thin or reactive
downtime or reliability burden aligns with the visible symptom
falsification_conditions: downtime and work-order history do not support the framing
allowed_claim_language: Maintenance maturity remains an admissible rival hypothesis that should be bounded before capital is framed as pure efficiency.
financial_exposure_if_true: CAPEX may target a secondary symptom
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to other dominant variables
stop_conditions: maintenance maturity is bounded enough to rank its economic relevance
escalation_conditions: operator or maintenance-manager confirmation required if documentary proof remains absent
claim_permissions_impact: block energy-only capital logic until maintenance reality is bounded
example_outputs: Maintenance may dominate economics before energy does; bound the reliability story before underwriting the retrofit story.
tests: manufacturing and warehouse cases with thin maintenance evidence should admit this as a rival explanation
pattern must remain non-diagnostic at L2
